chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Rifah said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man for whom travel becomes apparent during the month of Ramadan such that he reaches the morning (dawn). He said: 'He completes his fast for that day.'

I said: 'Indeed, he set out (started fasting) in the month of Ramadan, and there was only a midday portion of the day between him and his family (i.e., he was not yet far enough to be considered a traveler when dawn broke).' He said: 'When the dawn rises while he is still among his family, he has the choice: if he wishes, he fasts, and if he wishes, he breaks his fast.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who starts fasting at home and then leaves on a journey before dawn ends?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the specific ruling for a resident who departs on a journey after dawn has broken but before reaching the distance of qasr, granting them the choice (ikhtiyar) to either complete the fast as a resident or break it as a traveler. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the status at the time of fajr as the determining factor for the obligation, distinguishing this scenario from those who depart before dawn. This ruling underscores the flexibility in fiqh regarding the transition of travel status during the fasting day.
